c74object.name: evi_filter_bell
c74object.digest: evieve Gen Object. TPT peak/notch filter
c74object.description:
evi_filter_bell is an abstraction for using inside gen~ or GenExpr.
evi_filter_bell.gendsp requires the GenExpr file(s):
evi_svfs_tpt_filters.genexpr
evi_filter_bell is also available in MSP as: evi.filter.bell~.
The bell filter from the evieve TPT SVF collection. '...bandwidth at -3dB/+3dB from center freq'. Also with analog 'adaptive Q' option.

constructor.digest: { arguments={}, inlets={ input, cutoff, gain, q } }

geninlet.name: cutoff
geninlet.digest: in Hz @min 1 @max samplerate*0.5. Cutoff frequency in Hz.

geninlet.name: gain
geninlet.digest: in dB @min -30 @max 30 @default 0. ± gain in dB. The effect of gain depends on the @adaptive attribute.

geninlet.name: q
geninlet.digest: @min 0.05 @max 20 @default 0.707107. Q, clamped in the range 0.05..20. The effect of Q depends on the @adaptive attribute.

attribute.name: adaptive
attribute.description: Off by default means that the response of the filter will be like that of a classic RBJ peak/notch. If @adaptive is on the gain of the filter affects the Q of the filter whereby higher gain will cause steeper Q and vica versa. This is as would be the case in an analog filter.

attribute.name: smooth
attribute.description: Smooth the mixing gains of the filter efficiently at the core of the DSP. With these TPT SVF filters this will usually be the only smoothing required. By default smoothing is off.
